report:
## Conclusion: Your view is well-supported — ivermectin does not appear to lower the risk of death in COVID-19.

The strongest, highest-quality evidence consistently shows no mortality benefit from ivermectin in COVID-19 patients.

### Key evidence:

**1. Cochrane Systematic Review (2022):** The gold-standard Cochrane review concluded there is *"no evidence to support the use of ivermectin for treating COVID-19 or preventing SARS-CoV-2 infection,"* noting the evidence base, while improved, remains limited. (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD015017_ivermectin-preventing-and-treating-covid-19)

**2. ACTIV-6 Large RCT (October 2022):** A large randomized controlled trial published in 2022 found ivermectin was not effective as a COVID-19 treatment. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivermectin_during_the_COVID-19_pandemic)

**3. Systematic review and meta-analysis (BMC Infectious Diseases, 2022):** This review of RCTs found that ivermectin's benefit in reducing mortality *"cannot be concluded with confidence,"* and noted that several early studies suggesting benefit were retracted or had methodological problems. (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12879-022-07589-8)

**4. Recent meta-analysis (2024):** Found that although ivermectin alleviated some symptoms, it *"did not significantly improve critical clinical outcomes like mortality, ICU admissions, or ventilator use."* (https://www.ovid.com/jnls/annals-of-medicine-and-surgery/fulltext/10.1097/ms9.0000000000002762~the-impact-of-ivermectin-on-covid-19-outcomes-a-systematic)

### Evidence on the other side:

Early in the pandemic, some small RCTs and meta-analyses (e.g., a 2021 meta-analysis in *Therapeutics and Clinical Risk Management*) suggested a mortality reduction, but these were based on small, often low-quality studies — some later retracted for fraud. As larger, well-designed trials (ACTIV-6, PRINCIPLE, TOGETHER) reported results, the apparent benefit disappeared. The WHO and FDA both recommend against ivermectin for COVID-19 outside of clinical trials.

**Bottom line:** The best available evidence — large RCTs and high-quality systematic reviews — does not support ivermectin as a treatment that reduces COVID-19 mortality.
